question: Does drinking coffee make people live longer?

claims.text: In large observational cohorts, moderate coffee drinkers have somewhat lower all-cause mortality than non-drinkers.
Whether starting to drink coffee would extend a given person's life is not identifiable from those studies alone; healthier people may simply drink more coffee.
causal_assumptions: no unmeasured confounding by baseline health
no reverse causation from illness to quitting
defeaters: coffee drinking tracks income and activity

claims.text: A randomised trial of coffee over decades would settle the interventional question; none of that length exists.

checks_run: claims compared against the cited cohort analyses

limits: This answer does not cover specific medical conditions; ask a clinician about those.
